title: Convergence slate and launch credit allocation for cross-product rollouts
creator: Asha Raman
description: Create a lightweight operational model and tooling pattern ("launch credits") that ties roadmap priorities and OKR commitment to concrete capacity reservations and guardrails across runtime, console, and API release trains. The goal is to reduce ad-hoc capacity contention during multi-surface launches by allocating a small, fungible credit pool per initiative that teams can spend for reserved Dedicated capacity, priority canaries, or accelerated rollout windows.
background: Recent Q4 launches exposed frequent conflicts between Console experiments, Runtime kernel rollouts, and API schema changes. These conflicts manifested as competing canary windows and surprise capacity spikes that forced last-minute rollbacks or throttles. Leadership requested a plan to align OKR commitments with predictable runway and to make launch costs/risks explicit during roadmap planning.
goals: Provide a quantifiable ledger that maps OKR/initiative weight to reserve credits
Enable PMs and Eng leads to reserve time-bound capacity windows during planning
Reduce last-minute cross-team escalations by 50% in first two quarters after rollout
Instrument credits so spend becomes a signal for roadblock coaching and prioritization trade-offs
acceptance_criteria: Spec document reviewed and approved by Runtime, Console, and API leads
Prototype launch-credit ledger implemented in the Launch Planner dashboard
Two pilot initiatives (one Runtime-heavy, one Console-heavy) complete reservation and consumption cycle
Migration playbook for existing queued launches to use credits is documented
notes: 2026-03-01 Asha Raman: Draft proposal created. Outline includes credit sizing formula (OKR weight x dev intensity) and two consumption buckets: capacity-reserve and priority-canary.

2026-03-04 Diego Morales: Met with Runtime Eng (Leila Khan) and Console PM (Marco Silva). Runtime prefers credits to map to reserved GPU-hours; Console needs time-boxed console-ops windows. Agreed on two resource types for v1.

2026-03-07 Leila Khan (ENG): Raised concern about fragmentation of Dedicated pools. Trade-off: larger shared credit pool vs per-team pockets. Action: run simulation on historical launches to quantify collisions.
2026-03-09 Data team: Historical simulation scheduled; initial results due 2026-03-15. Early signal: 12% of launches accounted for 60% of unexpected capacity use.
2026-03-11 PM review: Added requirement that credits expire at quarter boundary and that overflow triggers ASAP-degrade policy (throttle non-critical canaries).
2026-03-12 Diego Morales: Approved prototype spec; assigned ENG-ops to build dashboard mock and a CLI reservation flow. Next: pilot pairing with SRE for incident playbook integration.
implementation_timeline: Week 1: Finalize credit sizing formula and resource buckets
Week 2: Build Launch Planner mock and ledger data model (readonly for pilots)
Week 3: Pilot reservations with two initiatives, capture consumption metrics
Week 4: Iterate on UX, add automated expiration and overflow rules, document playbook
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Teams hoard credits and underutilize capacity -> Mitigation: monthly unused credit reclamation and visibility
Risk: Credit reservations add friction to fast-moving squads -> Mitigation: lightweight fast-path (small instant-credit allotment) for experiments
Risk: Measurement mismatch between reserved and actual runtime usage -> Mitigation: billing-grade reconciliation pipeline and SRE alerting
next_steps: Deliver Launch Planner mock to Design and ENG by 2026-03-19
Schedule pilot pairings and SRE runbook rehearsal for week of 2026-03-22
